title: Decoupling Analog Circuit Representation from Technology for Behavior-Centric Optimization
problem: Analog IC design is strongly coupled with technology nodes and difficult to represent via abstract behavioral models; lack of accurate and efficient analog modeling hampers design automation, especially when porting designs across technologies.
motivation: Analog design automation is largely manual and expensive; behavior-centric, technology-agnostic approaches could unlock automation similar to digital design.
method: Proposes behavior-centric optimization framework representing circuit behavior via transistor electrical properties rather than sizes, improving generalization across technologies; develops method mapping electrical properties to device sizes; uses radial basis functions-based Kolmogorov-Arnold network (RBF-KAN) to approximate nonlinear circuit behavior with limited simulations.
key_novelty: Transistor electrical property-based circuit representation decoupled from technology nodes, enabling technology-agnostic surrogate modeling via RBF-KAN.
contributions: Behavior-centric circuit representation using transistor electrical properties vs. sizes
Method for mapping electrical properties to device sizes across technology nodes
RBF-KAN surrogate modeling for accurate nonlinear behavior approximation with few simulations
1.76×-2.64× improvement in large signal FOM; 1.73×-2.48× in small signal FOM
3.5×-6.2× acceleration in design porting across technologies

metrics.other: Large signal FOM: 1.76×-2.64× improvement; Small signal FOM: 1.73×-2.48× improvement

limitations: Evaluated on testing suite; portability to industrial analog IPs and validation across 5+ technology nodes not discussed.
primary_theme: Technology-agnostic analog circuit optimization via electrical property representation and RBF-KAN
